action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild age-appropriate atrophy and Fazekas 1 punctate white matter foci; no ventriculomegaly, no basal ganglia infarct or lacune; normal midbrain, pons and cerebellum; no mass or hemorrhage
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI to exclude a structural, vascular or atypical-parkinsonism cause
action_criteria.rationale: PD is a clinical diagnosis; MRI is normal in PD and excludes vascular lesions, NPH, mass and the midbrain, pontine and putaminal signs of PSP and MSA [Postuma_2015]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No dopamine receptor blocker; the bladder antimuscarinic flagged for central anticholinergic burden with peripherally acting or beta-3 agonist options; the calcium-channel blocker flagged for standing blood pressure
action_criteria.label: Review the medication list before starting dopaminergic treatment
action_criteria.rationale: No dopamine-blocking drug is on her list, but oxybutynin is a centrally acting anticholinergic and amlodipine lowers standing blood pressure; both matter once levodopa is started [Postuma_2015]

prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol or other centrally acting D2-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics; if an antipsychotic is needed, use quetiapine or clozapine
Do not start a centrally acting anticholinergic (trihexyphenidyl, benztropine) for the tremor: it adds to the anticholinergic burden of her bladder treatment and to confusion risk
required_recommendations: Diagnose clinically probable PD (MDS 2015): bradykinesia with decrement and right-predominant rest tremor and rigidity, no absolute exclusion, no red flag; the response to levodopa may add a supportive criterion [Postuma_2015]

Start carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg, half a tablet three times daily with food, increasing over 2 to 4 weeks to one tablet three times daily (300 mg/day levodopa), and review the response after 2 to 3 months [NICE_NG71]
If a dopamine agonist is used, warn about impulse control disorders and excessive daytime sleepiness and ask about them at every visit [NICE_NG71]
Replace oxybutynin with trospium or mirabegron: it is a centrally acting anticholinergic that adds to confusion and hallucination risk with dopaminergic treatment and worsens her constipation
Refer to physiotherapy for gait, turning and the recent near-fall, occupational therapy for fine-motor tasks, and speech and language therapy for the hypophonia [NICE_NG71]

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure, episodic confusion or encephalopathy: EEG does not inform this parkinsonism
No inflammatory, infectious or rapidly progressive feature: CSF has no role in this typical parkinsonism
No murmur, heart failure or cardiac symptom: an echocardiogram does not inform the parkinsonism
No syncope or palpitations; the near-fall was a loss of balance on turning: rhythm monitoring is not indicated
No cardiac symptom, syncope or QT-relevant drug planned: an ECG does not inform the parkinsonism
DaT SPECT is indicated when tremor cannot be clinically separated from parkinsonism; here the clinical diagnosis is clear and the scan would not change management [NICE_NG71]
Formal autonomic testing is not part of the PD work-up; bedside orthostatic measurement suffices

differential.key_features: Rest tremor that diminishes with action, bradykinesia with decrement and rigidity; her father's late-onset ET is a separate condition
No dopamine receptor blocker, antiemetic or antipsychotic exposure; asymmetric signs
Upper-limb predominant asymmetric onset, no stepwise course, and only Fazekas 1 foci without basal ganglia infarct or lacune on MRI
Overactive bladder for 5 years without incontinence is common at her age; no orthostatic symptoms, no cerebellar signs, rest tremor present, normal pons and cerebellum on MRI
Full vertical eye movements, no falls (one near-fall, pull test one step with self-correction), limb more than axial rigidity, normal midbrain on MRI

key_clinical_evidence: Right-predominant bradykinesia with decrement, 4-5 Hz pill-rolling rest tremor (milder on the left), cogwheel rigidity, micrographia, hypophonia and hypomimia: MDS 2015 parkinsonism
Rest tremor is the one supportive criterion before any levodopa trial; no red flag and no absolute exclusion: clinically probable PD
One near-fall without a fall and a pull test of one step with self-correction; no orthostatic symptoms or incontinence
MRI normal for age with Fazekas 1 foci: no vascular, structural or atypical-parkinsonism features
Oxybutynin is a centrally acting anticholinergic that matters once dopaminergic treatment starts

alternatives: Pramipexole or ropinirole (dopamine agonists), titrated gradually
Rasagiline 1 mg daily (MAO-B inhibitor) as monotherapy in mild disease
contraindications: Non-selective MAO inhibitors (phenelzine, tranylcypromine) with levodopa: risk of hypertensive crisis. Not on the current list.
interactions: Oxybutynin is a centrally active anticholinergic: it adds to confusion and hallucination risk with dopaminergic treatment in older patients. Trospium or mirabegron are alternatives.
Oxybutynin also slows gut transit and adds to constipation.

Amlodipine lowers standing blood pressure and adds to the orthostatic fall; levodopa can lower it further. Review the need for each and measure lying and standing blood pressure at each levodopa dose step.
warnings: Metformin and low-dose aspirin: no clinically relevant interaction with levodopa.
Iron salts and high-protein meals reduce levodopa absorption; if iron is added, give it at least 2 hours apart from levodopa.
Nausea is common at initiation; taking the dose with a small carbohydrate snack helps.
Dopaminergic drugs can cause excessive daytime sleepiness and sudden sleep onset: counsel about driving.
Impulse control disorders (gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping) occur mainly with dopamine agonists.
Mirabegron can raise blood pressure: check it after starting.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Classic asymmetric tremor-onset parkinsonism; the management point is her oxybutynin, and the father's ET and shoulder stiffness attributed to arthritis are distractors; 1 required criterion (MRI)
key_educational_points: Parkinson disease is diagnosed clinically based on the presence of bradykinesia plus resting tremor or rigidity
Asymmetric onset is a hallmark of idiopathic PD and helps distinguish it from drug-induced and vascular parkinsonism
Brain MRI is typically normal in PD but is important to exclude structural causes and features of atypical parkinsonism
DaTscan confirms presynaptic dopaminergic deficit but does not distinguish PD from atypical parkinsonian syndromes
A positive levodopa response is a supportive diagnostic criterion and guides treatment

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Crystal Morris is a 62-year-old right-handed retired high school principal who presents to the neurology outpatient clinic accompanied by her wife, Maria, for evaluation of a progressive right hand tremor and generalized slowing of movement over the past 18 months. Her wife first noticed the tremor in her right hand approximately a year and a half ago while they were watching television in the evening. She observed her right hand shaking while it rested on her lap, and it would stop when she reached for the remote control. Over the subsequent months, the tremor has become more persistent and now occurs throughout the day, though it remains most prominent at rest. Her wife also reports that her handwriting has become noticeably smaller and more cramped over the past year, to the point where she can barely read her grocery lists anymore. Ms. Morris herself has noticed that buttoning her shirts has become increasingly difficult, especially with her right hand, and shaving takes much longer than it used to. She describes a pervasive sense of stiffness in her right arm and shoulder that she initially attributed to arthritis. Over the past six to eight months, her wife has noticed that she walks more slowly with a slight shuffle and that her right arm no longer swings naturally when she walks. She had one near-fall two months ago when she turned quickly to answer the telephone and lost her balance briefly, catching herself on the kitchen counter. She has not had any frank falls. Her wife has also noted that her facial expression seems less animated than before, and her voice has become quieter. She reports mild constipation over the past year and occasional difficulty staying asleep, though she denies vivid dreams or acting out in her sleep. She denies any cognitive difficulties beyond occasional word-finding pauses, which her wife confirms are no different from baseline. She has not experienced visual hallucinations, orthostatic lightheadedness, or urinary incontinence. Her mood has been slightly subdued, but she denies frank depression or anxiety.

neurological_exam.additional: Glabellar tap reflex positive (Myerson sign). Seborrhea noted on the forehead and nasolabial folds. Micrographia demonstrated when asked to write a sentence. No myoclonus. No apraxia. No alien limb phenomenon.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing normal bilaterally. Heel-to-shin testing normal bilaterally. Rapid alternating movements are slow and decremental on the right, with progressive reduction in amplitude (bradykinesia). Left hand shows subtle decrement on repetitive finger tapping.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Facial expression is notably decreased bilaterally (masked facies), more prominent on the right. Hearing grossly intact bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline without fasciculations.
neurological_exam.gait: Gait is slow with reduced right arm swing. Stride length is mildly shortened. Mild forward flexion of the trunk (stooped posture). Mild difficulty with turns, requiring 3-4 steps to complete a 180-degree turn (en bloc turning). Pull test shows 1 step retropulsion but self-corrects. No festination. Tandem gait is mildly impaired.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented to person, place, time, and situation. MMSE 28/30 (lost 1 point on recall at 5 minutes, 1 point on serial sevens). Speech is hypophonic with slightly monotone prosody but fluent and grammatically correct. Naming, repetition, and comprehension intact. Clock drawing normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Bulk normal throughout. Tone is increased in the right upper extremity with cogwheel rigidity at the wrist, and mild lead-pipe rigidity at the right elbow. Left upper extremity shows mild cogwheel rigidity at the wrist. Lower extremities show mildly increased tone bilaterally, right greater than left. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. No pronator drift. Right hand resting tremor at 4-5 Hz, pill-rolling in character, diminishes with action. Mild intermittent left hand resting tremor noted when patient is distracted during mental tasks.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric in biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles tendons bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, temperature, vibration, and proprioception in all extremities.
